source.title: How Deep Can LLMs Learn to Reason? Expressiveness Is Key
source.authors: Tianle Wang; Zhao-Yang Wang; Guangchen Lan; Xinpeng Wei; Sipeng Zhang; Guanwen Qiu; Abulhair Saparov

page_placements.theme: Reinforcement-learning scaling depends on architecture, difficulty and allocation

record.file_problem: Full paper. Some figure text is OCR-garbled, but the relevant scaling results are also stated in prose and tables.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports its own RL-training-cost scaling against synthetic reasoning-task depth. It does not test pretraining held-out cross-entropy scaling against parameters, tokens, or compute, or compute-optimal parameter/token allocation.
record.gate_note: The paper cites prior language-model pretraining scaling-law studies, but its own scaling target is the RL training effort needed to reach a validation-accuracy threshold as proof depth or candidate count changes. These findings concern a related but different construct, so the rows are linked to none of V1–V7. The table reports the central depth-scaling fits and selected comparisons; downstream benchmark results are not rows because they do not measure predictable improvement with model scale or pretraining loss.
record.test_reason: The study fits RL post-training steps to reach 90% task accuracy against synthetic proof depth (T ∝ D^γ). It never measures held-out pretraining loss against parameters, tokens or compute, compute-optimal allocation, architecture shape, or downstream performance as a function of model scale or pretraining loss. V5 names fine-tuning regimes, but the scaled variable here is task difficulty, not training resources, so it is a related but different construct. Kaplan et al. appear only in citations and the FLOPs formula in Appendix G.3.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct in substance. Add that the authors also claim more expressive training yields larger, more compute-efficient downstream transfer (up to +10.66 points). They also say long-horizon reasoning limits are not fundamental to the architecture. They frame the power law as an empirical description of the observed depth range, not an asymptotic law.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains models with RL on synthetic logical reasoning tasks and measures steps to reach a validation-accuracy threshold as proof depth changes. It does not use the original pretraining-loss measurement or compute-optimal allocation procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported RL training-step exponent varies with logical expressiveness and training distribution; the paper also reports different exponents across RL algorithms and model configurations.

fits_no_version.finding: RL training steps to reach 90% held-out accuracy follow T ∝ D^γ in proof depth, with R² > 0.99. γ rises with logical expressiveness, from 1.05 to 2.60 (Qwen3-4B), and replicates on Qwen3-8B (0.99–2.53) and on Ministral3-3B.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: RL post-training cost to reach a fixed accuracy scales as a power law in reasoning depth, with an exponent set by task expressiveness.

fits_no_version.finding: The fitted depth exponent depends on training distribution (curriculum 1.33, uniform 1.70, difficult-only 2.36) and on RL algorithm (GRPO 2.05 vs DAPO 1.70 and GSPO 1.65). It also shifts with compute metric, e.g. 2.60 to 3.12 for FLOPs at + Quantification (Table 6), and with the accuracy threshold (Table 5).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: RL difficulty-scaling exponents depend on training distribution, optimizer and compute accounting.

record.problems: The authors state that main scaling curves use limited depth values and mostly single-seed runs; they characterize the power law as an empirical description of the observed regime rather than an established asymptotic law. Broader multi-seed validation is needed, and the generality of some comparisons across all expressiveness settings is unverified. The study does not measure the pretraining-loss, parameter-count, token-count, or compute-optimal-allocation quantities in the claim.
record.rows_left_out: Not extracted: appendix robustness fits for alternative compute measures, the 85% threshold, prompt-length reparameterization, operator swaps, candidate-count scaling, and additional ablations. These concern RL task-depth/candidate-count training costs rather than any stated claim version; central main-text depth fits and selected distribution, algorithm, and model replications are retained.

untested.parts: Pretraining held-out loss versus parameters, tokens or compute: not measured.
Extrapolation of small-run loss fits to much larger runs: not measured.
Architecture shape effects on loss at fixed parameter count: not measured.
Loss or performance power laws in compute, data or parameters in other regimes: not measured. The RL fits are against task depth, not training resources.
Downstream performance versus model scale or pretraining loss: not measured. Downstream gains are reported against RL training steps and task expressiveness, with only one 4B-vs-8B downstream check.
Fit-dependence of pretraining scaling exponents or splits: not measured. The exponent sensitivity reported (threshold, compute metric, algorithm) concerns the RL-depth law.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's gate is right: all rows correctly carry ['none'] and cannot_determine is acceptable, since no row measures any version. r8 and r9 report the same pooled 3-seed uniform/DAPO fit (γ=1.70) and are duplicates. r2 is the single-seed main fit (1.67). The record gives r13 no R², but Figure 13 shows R²=0.984, which matches the text's 'R² ≥ 0.98'. Robustness tables (G.2–G.8) and candidate-count scaling (H.1) are reasonably left out; they bear on no version.

relation.reason: Section 2 discusses pretraining and RL scaling literature to distinguish its analysis of reasoning complexity.

tranche.reason: Training steps versus proof depth measures a different construct from V1–V7. The study neither tests nor uses the cataloged scaling laws.

source_check.notes: Appendix A limits the power-law interpretation to the observed depth range and notes single-seed main scaling curves. Steps versus task depth does not establish any cataloged claim version.

statements.correction: T = RL steps to 90% held-out Pass@1. Qwen3-4B: γ increases from 1.05 to 2.60; all five R²>0.99 (Table 4). Qwen3-8B: γ increases from 0.99 to 2.53; all five R²≥0.98; + Conjunction R²=0.984 (Figure 13; Appendix H.5).
statements.problem: The exponent ranges are correct, but the unqualified R²>0.99 does not hold across both models: Qwen3-8B + Conjunction has R²=0.984.
